items.title: Kyiv Post: Russia keeps up strikes while a limited humanitarian truce is announced for Oleshky
items.summary: Kyiv Post's live page for 24 October and an AP-based search summary report continued Russian missile and drone attacks, including a Kramatorsk airstrike that killed one civilian and wounded six. Separately, a White House statement cited in coverage says a localized humanitarian truce in occupied Oleshky is due to begin on 29 October. Details of the truce are unconfirmed and early, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: Whether talks and local truces turn into a wider ceasefire drives energy prices and sanctions risk that global employers plan hiring around.

items.title: Jio Platforms IPO closed heavily subscribed; allotment on 26 October, listing set for 28 October
items.summary: Trendlyne and Chittorgarh list the Rs 30,213 crore Jio Platforms issue, priced at Rs 1,065 to 1,119 a share, as closing on 23 October with allotment on 26 October and listing on BSE and NSE on 28 October. One tracker puts final subscription at 22.19 times, but figures differ across sources and are provisional. Unofficial grey-market quotes near Rs 243 to 246 are indicative only and not a guarantee of listing price.
items.why: A mega consumer-tech listing shows how markets price brand scale and subscriber loyalty, a useful lens for marketing strategy.

items.title: India and Poland aim to double trade by 2030 and open a defence industry dialogue
items.summary: Reported on 22 October (three days ago): after talks between PM Modi and Polish PM Donald Tusk in New Delhi, the two sides set a target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 and agreed a Defence Industry Dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue. No fresher India story with a verifiable link was found today.
items.why: Trade targets open export and market-entry roles in engineering, defence supply chains and consumer goods that recruit MBAs.

items.title: Cursor adds Computer Use so its coding agents can operate any desktop app
items.summary: AI Weekly's daily digest for 24 October lists Cursor's Computer Use, announced on 23 October, which lets its agents click and type across desktop applications rather than only the browser. The same digest lists Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro release, with open weights promised by 4 November. These are company announcements and not independently tested.
items.why: Agents that operate ordinary software change which HR and marketing tasks can be automated, so skills planning needs to catch up.

items.title: Universal Music licenses its catalogs to AI music platform Tyger
items.summary: AI Weekly reports on 23 October that Universal Music Group became the first major music company to license its recorded and publishing catalogs to Tyger, an AI music platform.
items.why: Licensing deals are the template brands will follow for AI-generated content rights.
